steps.say: The wetting solution is carrying three drugs in fixed amounts. One litre of saline is holding five hundred to one thousand milligrams of lidocaine with one milligram of epinephrine and ten milliequivalents of bicarbonate. Numbness, vessel constriction, and sting relief are arriving together.
steps.tx: **Klein tumescent** formula (the standard wetting solution) consists of **1** liter normal saline with **500** to **1000** mg **lidocaine** (the numbing agent), **1** mg **epinephrine** (the vessel constrictor) at 1 to 1,000,000 dilution, and **10** mEq **sodium bicarbonate** (the sting buffer). Three drugs, one bag, fixed ratios.

steps.say: Tumescent dosing is running far above normal limits. Thirty five to fifty five milligrams per kilogram is staying safe under tumescence, against only seven milligrams per kilogram for standard lidocaine with epinephrine. Extreme dilution plus clamped vessels is explaining the difference.
steps.tx: The tumescent **lidocaine dose** runs **35** to **55** mg per kg, while ordinary local anaesthesia with epinephrine caps at **7** mg per kg. Litres of dilute solution plus clamped vessels explain why tumescence bends the normal ceiling so far. Weight-based math precedes every case.

steps.say: Blood levels are peaking hours after the case ends. Eight to fourteen hours is passing before serum lidocaine tops out, because profound vasoconstriction is holding the drug in fat. Overnight vigilance is matching the pharmacology.
steps.tx: Peak serum **lidocaine** concentrations occur **8** to **14** hours after tumescent infiltration due to delayed subcutaneous vascular absorption from profound **epinephrine vasoconstriction** (clamped vessels metering drug release). Dose math and monitoring must respect the delayed peak: the danger hour is midnight, not mid-operation.

rows: Watch the night, not just the table

steps.say: Toxicity is climbing a recognisable ladder. Perioral numbness with metallic taste and ringing ears is warning first. Slurred speech and seizures are following, then breathing and circulation are failing. Early rungs are triggering lipid rescue thinking.
steps.tx: **Lidocaine toxicity** (systemic local-anaesthetic poisoning) progresses from **perioral numbness** (lip tingling), **metallic taste**, and **tinnitus** (ear ringing), to **slurred speech**, **seizures**, **respiratory arrest** (breathing stops), and cardiovascular collapse. Each rung demands escalation; the early rung demands lipid emulsion readiness. Response teams keep lipid emulsion and airway kit at the bedside.

steps.say: Five litres is drawing the big-case line. Removing five thousand millilitres or more of total lipoaspirate is defining large-volume liposuction. Fat plus fluid is counting together, and overnight inpatient observation is becoming mandatory.
steps.tx: **Large-volume liposuction** **LVL** (big-case category) is defined as removal of **5000** mL or greater of total **lipoaspirate** (fat plus fluid together) in a single procedure, mandating overnight inpatient observation. Fluids, urine output, and haemoglobin are watched until morning; day-case shortcuts at this volume kill.

steps.say: Super-wet infiltration is matching fluid to fat one for one. One millilitre of fluid per millilitre of expected aspirate is keeping blood loss under one percent. True tumescent technique is using two to three times more fluid still.
steps.tx: Tumescent infiltration ratio in **super-wet** technique (balanced wetting method) is **1** mL of fluid per **1** mL of expected aspirate, with blood loss comprising less than **1%** of total aspirate volume. Epinephrine-blanched fat aspirates nearly bloodless; dry technique never matched this safety.

rows: Two to three times more fluid

steps.say: Deep buttock injections are sending fat to the lungs. Fatal pulmonary fat embolism is following intramuscular cannula passes that are lacerating gluteal veins. Hypoxaemia with brain dysfunction and petechiae is the same triad shown here, and subcutaneous placement is never producing it.
steps.tx: Fatal **pulmonary fat embolism** syndrome (fat blocking lung vessels) during **gluteal fat grafting** (Brazilian butt lift) is caused by deep **intramuscular injection** with the cannula and laceration of **gluteal venous** tributaries (buttock veins torn open). Fat entering torn veins embolises to lungs; strictly subcutaneous placement has never produced this syndrome.

vis.alt: Fat embolism syndrome triad with hypoxaemia, neurological dysfunction, and petechial rash after long-bone injury.
vis.caption: Fat embolism triad of hypoxaemia, brain dysfunction, and petechiae; the same picture kills in deep gluteal grafting. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Multi-society safety **guidelines** (joint plastic surgery edicts) mandate that fat grafting to the **gluteal** region (buttock augmentation) must be strictly confined to the **subcutaneous** space (the fat layer above fascia), strictly avoiding the **subfascial** or **intramuscular** planes. Ultrasound-guided subcutaneous delivery with blunt cannulas is the audited standard; deep passes kill.
steps.say: Only the surface fat layer is accepting graft. Multi-society guidance is confining gluteal fat strictly to the subcutaneous space. Subfascial and intramuscular planes are staying forbidden, and ultrasound-guided blunt delivery is defining the audited standard.
